review_comments.body: `emailAddress` can already contain a display name — the connector README documents `Logto<noreply@logto.io>` and `<noreply@logto.io>` — and this wraps it in another pair of angle brackets. With a template `sendFrom` of `Logto`, the request carries `FromEmailAddress: 'Logto <Logto<noreply@logto.io>>'` (or `Logto <<noreply@logto.io>>`), which SES rejects, so every send fails for a tenant configured as documented.

`replyTo` is checked before the handlebars are replaced, so a template that renders to an empty string still adds `ReplyToAddresses: ['']`. `replaceSendMessageHandlebars` returns an empty string when the payload has the root property but not the nested one, and SES rejects an empty reply-to address, so the whole send fails.

`includes('@')` treats a display name rendered from `{{application.name}}`, such as `Billing @ Acme Europe`, as a full address and drops the configured sender. The angle-bracket regex can also extract `EU` from a valid configuration like `"Platform <EU>" <noreply@example.com>`. Both produce an invalid `FromEmailAddress` for the verification email.

Could we reuse `parseSendFrom` from `@logto/connector-kit`, as SMTP2GO and MailJunky do, to parse the configured and template senders, then validate the extracted email with `z.string().email()`? For a name-only `sendFrom`, keep the configured mailbox and quote and escape the display name as needed when building the SES address, for example `"Acme, Inc." <noreply@example.com>`.

The display name is concatenated into `FromEmailAddress` without quoting or encoding. SES requires non-ASCII characters in the friendly name to be RFC 2047 encoded-word, so a localized `sendFrom` such as `Logto 团队` makes every email for that locale fail (or get its characters stripped). Names containing `,`, `(`, `"` etc. (e.g. `Acme, Inc.`) also need to be quoted, otherwise the header parses as multiple addresses and SES rejects it.

Treating any rendered `sendFrom` that contains `@` as a full address is fragile: `sendFrom` is documented as the sender's name alias, so a name like `Support @ Acme` becomes an invalid From and the send fails. Since handlebars are rendered first, a template using a user-controlled value (e.g. `{{user.name}}`) also lets that user set the From to any address on the verified domain.

comments.body:
Thanks for the review. Both points are fixed in the new commit:

- `getFromEmailAddress` now takes only the bare address from inside `<...>` when the configured `emailAddress` already has a display name, so `Logto<noreply@logto.io>` with `sendFrom: 'Foo'` gives `Foo <noreply@logto.io>` instead of nested brackets.
- `ReplyToAddresses` is omitted when `replyTo` renders to an empty string (e.g. a template variable with no value), instead of sending `['']`.

Added a test for each case; the connector's vitest suite and eslint pass.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Thanks both, these points are addressed in the new commit:

- `sendFrom` is now parsed with `parseSendFrom` from `@logto/connector-kit` (as SMTP2GO and MailJunky do) instead of `includes('@')` and the angle-bracket regex. `Billing @ Acme Europe` stays a display name, and `"Platform <EU>" <noreply@example.com>` is read as name plus address. The same parser is applied to the configured `emailAddress`, so `Logto<noreply@logto.io>` still works.
- An address that comes from the template is validated with `z.string().email()`; if it is not valid, the configured sender is used.
- For a name-only `sendFrom`, the configured mailbox is kept and the name is quoted/escaped when needed (`"Acme, Inc." <noreply@example.com>`). A non-ASCII name such as `Logto 团队` is sent as an RFC 2047 encoded-word.

On the point that a template value could set the From address: a full address in `sendFrom` is still honored, since that is what the i18n template field allows today. That means a template that interpolates a user-controlled field such as `{{user.name}}` can still pick another address on the verified domain. If you would rather keep the configured mailbox and use `sendFrom` only as the display name in this connector, say so and it will be changed in this PR.

Added tests for the quoting, the encoded-word, the bracketed name and the invalid-address fallback; the connector's vitest suite and eslint pass.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
